name: faer (dense linear algebra)
baseline: nalgebra (pure Rust, matrixmultiply backend) and ndarray with OpenBLAS, f64 column-major matrices
verdict_reason: faer is far faster than nalgebra on decompositions at n >= 64 (5.3x Cholesky, 13x SVD, 5.8x self-adjoint EVD at n = 1024), but single-threaded matrix multiply is only 1.15x faster, nalgebra wins on tiny matrices (n = 4), and OpenBLAS-backed ndarray beats single-threaded faer on SVD. The text tables are from April 2024; newer results are published only as charts.
tier_reason: First-party tables with the CPU named but no rustc version or flags for the Rust libraries; the 2025 benchmark pages are chart-only.
claimed_speedup: n = 1024, f64, times for faer / faer(par) / ndarray / nalgebra: matmul 33.9ms / 6.6ms / 9.7ms / 39.1ms; Cholesky 7.8ms / 3.4ms / 14.5ms / 41.2ms; SVD 297.8ms / 152ms / 253.8ms / 3.95s; self-adjoint EVD 132.1ms / 68.4ms / 909ms / 764.1ms (faer vs nalgebra 1.15x, 5.28x, 13.3x, 5.78x; parallel faer vs ndarray+OpenBLAS 1.47x, 4.26x, 1.67x, 13.3x) (derived from page data). n = 4 SVD: faer 2µs vs nalgebra 1.3µs
workload: Square f64 column-major matrices from n = 4 to 1024: matrix multiply, Cholesky, LU, QR, inverse, SVD and eigendecompositions; faer single-threaded and with 12 threads.
toolchain: Eigen compiled with -march=native -O3 -fopenmp; rustc version and Rust flags not stated
platforms: Pure Rust; SIMD kernels chosen at runtime through pulp's feature detection
one_liner: Pure-Rust dense linear algebra; 5-13x faster than nalgebra on large decompositions, about even on matmul and slower on tiny matrices.
how_it_is_fast: faer uses blocked, cache-aware decompositions that spend most of their time in matrix multiply, built on the gemm and nano-gemm kernels with runtime SIMD dispatch through pulp. nalgebra's decompositions are textbook unblocked loops, which is why the gap grows with n.
use_it_when: You factor or decompose matrices of n >= 64 (Cholesky, LU, QR, SVD, EVD) in pure Rust.
You want parallel dense linear algebra without linking a BLAS/LAPACK.
skip_it_when: Your matrices are small and fixed-size (2x2 to 4x4); nalgebra's static types are as fast or faster there.
You only need matrix multiply; single-threaded faer is within 15% of nalgebra.
You already link a tuned LAPACK through ndarray-linalg for SVD-heavy work.
caveats: The text tables come from the README as of April 2024 (faer 0.18 era); faer is now 0.24, and the current benchmark pages (2025-09-22, Ryzen 7 8745HS and Xeon Gold 6146) show results only as log-scale charts, so the current gap cannot be quoted.
ndarray was measured through OpenBLAS, which is multi-threaded by default, while plain faer columns are single-threaded; compare faer(par) with ndarray.
Benchmarks are first-party and give no Rust compiler version or RUSTFLAGS.
tradeoffs: Larger dependency tree and longer compile times than nalgebra (gemm, pulp, generic code over many scalar types).
Frequent breaking API changes between 0.x releases.

evidence.quote: The benchmarks were run on an `11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-11400 @ 2.60GHz` with 12 threads.
